# The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
# flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built and builds them with the game waiting: those
# above the first "section" line before the game starts, and a section when a frame first draws with 4 of its shaders,
# so that nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's README, "Give
# RT64 a list of the game's shaders").
#
# Recorded by code, not by playing: bash tools/record_shaders.sh (its header says how) runs N64Recomp-browser's
# tools/record_shaders.mjs with tools/shader_plan.json, which loads the page fresh for each section and has
# tools/shader_survey.js start each place from the game's own checkpoint table and each multiplayer mode against bots.
# Section 0 is the launcher, the logos, the intro, the bar and its menus (GAME1, MULTI with the barrels and the mode
# list, OPTIONS, CHAPTERS). Then a section a chapter, each of its places reached from the checkpoint table (Hungover
# with the new game's opening; Windy; Barn Boys; Bats Tower with the boiler; Sloprano; Uga Buga; Spooky; It's War, in
# two, "war" and its second half "war-tank"; The Heist), a few seconds of each, skipping the cutscene, walking,
# turning the camera, jumping and the pause menu. Places that draw shaders their chapter's others don't are played
# again in a load of their own, on foot after the cutscene for 20 s, or 40 s in a boss fight: out and back by as much,
# jumping, attacking, crouching and turning the camera (Barn Boys' checkpoint 50; Poovarotti Flush; Spooky's
# checkpoint 171; A Tank Too Far and War Boss Countdown; Fight The Alien). Then a section for each of seven
# multiplayer modes, one player against three bots. Not recorded: the multiplayer Race (it goes back to the bar when
# started this way), split screen, the Options screens, and whatever the other places draw further in than their
# start; RT64 builds those when the game first asks for them. The last section, "earlier", is what an earlier
# recording by hand had that this one never printed. Flags follow settings (filtering, HDR, MSAA, upscaling), so a
# change to one of those defaults means recording again.
